newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss refuse visa to Zaire's Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Swiss refuse visa to Zaire's Mobutu.

text.p: Switzerland has denied a visa to Zaire's ailing ruler Mobutu Sese Seko, who is currently in France and wants to return to the country for medical treatment, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said on Monday.
Spokesman Hans Ruedi Bortis told Reuters: "There was a new request (from Mobutu) for a visa. This request will not be accepted. A visa will not be granted."
Mobutu, 66, underwent more than two months of treatment for prostate cancer in Lausanne, Switzerland before leaving on November 4 for the French Riviera where he has a villa.
The Zairean ruler said later that he intended to return to Lausanne for a medical check-up.
Bortis said Mobutu's departure meant the medical grounds for a possible extension of his Swiss visa no longer existed.

"From the point of view of the Swiss Foreign Ministry, with the departure of Mr Mobutu, the medical reason for a new visa does not exist any more. We do not have to explain further why we do not issue a new visa," he said.
Swiss official sources said Mobutu had applied for a new Swiss visa on Friday.
Mobutu's absence from Zaire has raised fears that his vast central African country may disintegrate following a successful Tutsi revolt in the east.

His presence in Switzerland sparked protests from local deputies in Lausanne who appealed to the federal government to block his return. Privately, police and other officials breathed a sigh of relief when he packed up and left.

Mobutu told French TF-1 television last week that he planned to undergo a three-day check-up in Switzerland, where he is reported by Swiss media to have more than $4 billion in numbered bank accounts, and then return to his strife-torn country.

In France, Mobutu has received officials of several governments involved in the creation of an international force to rescue hundreds of thousands of mostly-Rwandan refugees fleeing a Tutsi revolt in eastern Zaire.
In Lausanne, Swiss secrecy and discreet security surrounded the Zairean strongman, whose visitors included France's former interior minister, Charles Pasqua.
